hints: Hint 1: Compare the size and wall thickness of the three labels. Label 1 is a large oval space with a distinct thicker wall, label 2 is one of the many thin-walled empty spaces, and label 3 is a small round structure filled with cells.

Hint 2: Remember what each lung structure looks like in section. Air-conducting tubes have an epithelial wall with muscle, gas-exchange spaces have extremely thin squamous walls, and blood vessels have thicker muscular walls containing red blood cells.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Look at label 2 first, the background tissue**
Most of the photomicrograph is made of large, empty-looking polygonal spaces with very thin walls. This is classic spongy lung tissue.

These are alveoli, the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens. Their walls are one cell thick to give a short diffusion distance.

Step 2: **Identify label 1, the large oval airway**
Label 1 is much larger than a single alveolus and has a clearly thicker, darker-staining wall all around it. It is empty because it contains air, not blood.

This is a bronchiole, a small air-conducting tube. It is lined by epithelium with some smooth muscle, so its wall looks much more substantial than an alveolar wall.

Step 3: **Identify label 3, the small filled vessel**
Label 3 is small, round, has a thick wall and is packed with dark-staining cells (red blood cells). It sits right next to the bronchiole, which is typical.

This is a small artery (a branch of the pulmonary arteriole system) carrying deoxygenated blood to the lungs. A capillary would be tiny, just wide enough for one red cell, in the alveolar wall, not this large thick-walled structure. So 1 is bronchiole, 2 is alveolus, 3 is small artery, which is row C.

options.A: Incorrect because label 1 is far too large with too thick a wall to be an alveolus, and label 3 is too large and thick-walled to be a capillary.
options.B: Incorrect because label 1 is an air tube (bronchiole), not an alveolus, and label 3 is a blood vessel with muscle wall, not an air tube.
options.C: Correct. Label 1 is the bronchiole with its epithelial and muscle wall, label 2 is the thin-walled alveolus, and label 3 is the small artery with thick wall and blood cells.
options.D: Incorrect because label 1 is empty and air-filled (bronchiole), not blood-filled, and label 3 is blood-filled (small artery), not air-filled.
